Third review, live on rootless Podman 4.9.3 with Renovate 44.226.2. network now takes none or a plain name: host, container, ns, private, bridge, default, slirp4netns and pasta are refused in any case, as is anything with ':', '=', ',' or '/'; a definition made earlier with network host is refused when run. `host.` and `Default.` pass the pattern and Podman reads them as network names that do not exist, not as modes. Planted again at logLevel info and debug: hostRules tokens and passwords, a tracked .npmrc, the npmrc option, user:password in registryUrls, .env and .git/config were found in nothing swamp keeps or prints. passProxy on an engine that is not Podman now logs that nothing is passed (shown with a stand-in binary that reports a Docker version). README says that Renovate repeats a refused configuration value.

Reviewed the tests against ef7f107. The strict fake container engine and most negative tests are gone (89 unit tests then, 25 now). lookup, the one method, runs through createModelTestContext with a stub at lib/cli.ts's __setSpawn that answers only listed prefixes and rejects any other call, restored in a finally: a run that records a repository and the inventory with Renovate's warnings logged, a run that exits non-zero recorded as failed and counted, and an image not held with pull never, which fails before any container and writes nothing. The pure parts keep their tests, including proxySecrets, data names, network refusal, configuration files that are links, directories, devices or FIFOs, and package.json bounds. The planted secrets, hanging runs, cancellation and hostile output that the unit suite covered before are now covered only by the live suite in smoke/ (engine.sh plants a proxy password and checks it is nowhere; fixtures.sh plants a value in a refused configuration), which the previous review relied on as well; no unit test plants the proxy password in lookup's records. Acceptable given the live suite. README and smoke/README.md now say so honestly.

The blocking finding of the second review is fixed: a `renovate` key in package.json gives configRead package.json and status ok (shown live), and one that says enabled false is failed with disabled-by-config. The three proof lines held against forgery, in one Git directory with an untracked renovate.json that Renovate did not read: each of the three lines as a whole JSON line and as bare text in a Dockerfile comment, in dependency names with line breaks, as the name and description of a package.json without a renovate key, and as names of tracked files; the record stayed config-not-read. In the raw debug output of that run the only message carrying repository text was 'npm file package.json has name "..."', which the anchored pattern `^Found (\S+) config file$` cannot match, and no other message of Renovate 44.226.2 has that shape ('Found npm package files', 'Found 5 package file(s)' do not). Two small things README does not say, neither wrong in the record: (1) README 'Configuration' says a configuration Git does not track is not read; that holds for the configuration files, but an untracked package.json with a renovate key in a Git directory is read by Renovate (shown: its enabled false was obeyed) and the record says so truthfully with configRead package.json. (2) README does not say what a network name that does not exist gives: each repository failed with the engine's 'network not found', the method succeeds. One sentence each would do.
